Language Proficiency

Python 3

I would consider python 3 to be my most proficienct language. I use python for pretty much every back-end job (except front-end logic). My strength definitely resides in data structures and algorithms and python makes that very simple.

Java

Java would definitely be my second most proficienct language. Not a big fan of the syntax but I have gotten used to it over the years. I use java mostly for game and application creation.

Javascript/Typescript

My javascript knowledge pretty much ends at the required proficiency for react. I would like to know more javascript, but it seems that I'm typically doing back-end work most of the time and python is my go-to for that.

React

My overrall react skills are fairly proficient. I know how to get around the interface and implement components, but my large-scale production needs some work. Although, I can see myself improving in the things I lack in react.

C++

C++ is a language I've always wanted to learn. The language always appearead difficuly and different from the languages I'm used so there's no doubt in saying I'm definitely not very proficienct However I can definitely see myself learning it in the future.

Go

Like C++, I've always wanted to learn Go. I don't really have any reason to learn it as of now,and so I've put it on the backburner. However, I really do see myself getting into it in the next couple of years.

C#

Once more, C# is a language I want to learn. However, due to the tedious nature of game design, I've also put it on the back burner so I really have no reason to learn C#. However, if I ever get into game design, there is no doubt that I will learn C#.

SQL

SQL is probably next up for me. I really need to get going with database languages. I have no reason not to learn it and now is a great time to start. I expect myself to be fairly proficient in SQL by mid-next year.

) } export default Proficiency;
